page: Microsoft Azure FX32-8mds_v2 is a specialized compute- and memory-oriented virtual machine powered by Microsoft Hyper-V. The instance runs on an Intel Xeon 8573C processor using the x86_64 architecture, configured with 4 dedicated physical cores yielding 8 vCPUs at a high base clock of 4.2 GHz. Backed by 260 MB of L3 cache, the system includes Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 vector support. Hardware provisioning features a substantial 672.0 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation of 84.0 GB per vCPU, coupled with a 1890 GB local NVMe SSD. No dedicated graphics accelerators are present, and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are supplied by default.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate standout single-threaded compute capability alongside standard multi-threaded capacity bounded by the 8-vCPU configuration. The instance achieves a top-tier Geekbench single-core score of 2352.0 and high single-threaded compression throughput, reaching 34.73 GB/sec in gzip testing. In contrast, multi-core benchmarks such as stress-ng (8876.24) and Geekbench multi-core (8736.0) fall squarely into average mid-range bands due to the core count. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 71.78 GB/sec with write speeds of 52.07 GB/sec. Complex tasks like local LLM token generation degrade into lower percentiles, producing 7.72 tokens/sec on 7B models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the FX32-8mds_v2 presents a distinct hardware tradeoff: it prioritizes extreme per-core memory density and high clock frequencies over raw aggregate core count. This architecture reduces software licensing costs pegged to core metrics while providing the high-speed scratch space of local NVMe storage. Workloads that match this profile include large in-memory databases, electronic design automation (EDA), relational database management systems requiring large buffer pools, and memory-constrained analytical data pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure FX32-8mds_v2 is a high-frequency, memory-dense virtual machine built for specialized enterprise workloads. Driven by a 4.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8573C processor, the instance supplies 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores, 260 MB of L3 cache, and support for AVX-512 and AMX instructions. It features an expansive 672.0 GB of RAM, delivering an exceptional 84.0 GB per vCPU, paired with 1890 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage. In benchmark evaluations, the server achieves top-tier single-core CPU throughput and strong single-threaded data compression, while multi-core compute and uncached memory bandwidth align with mid-range baselines. Without bundled GPUs, machine learning generation is constrained. The instance represents an efficient infrastructure profile for memory-heavy, per-core-licensed systems, such as in-memory databases, high-performance caching nodes, electronic design automation, and intensive data batch processing.
